protocol.read_scoring: Correct if normalize(model answer) equals normalize(answer) or normalize(any alias). normalize = Unicode NFKC, drop a backslash that precedes ASCII punctuation (Markdown escapes such as 'locked\_out\_user'), map any Unicode dash to '-', trim, collapse internal whitespace to one space, strip one trailing '.', casefold. A null or missing answer is incorrect.
protocol.act_scoring: The answer is resolved to a live element in the same page load the representation came from (see METHODOLOGY.md, 'Answer resolution'). Correct if and only if it resolves to exactly the ground-truth element. Answers that match several elements without a disambiguating occurrence, invalid selectors or roles, unknown indices or refs, and malformed JSON are incorrect, each with its own recorded reason.
protocol.reply_parsing: The reply text is stripped of surrounding whitespace and of one surrounding ``` or ```json fence, then parsed with json.loads. Anything that is not a JSON object is scored incorrect with reason malformed_json. {"answer": null} is scored incorrect with reason no_answer.
protocol.error_accounting: Each (repeat, page, task, representation) is called exactly once. API errors and timeouts (120 s) are not retried; they are scored incorrect, kept in every accuracy denominator, and also counted separately.
protocol.token_accounting: representation_tokens = count_tokens(full prompt) - count_tokens(same prompt with an empty page slot); fixed_prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt with an empty page slot). Both via the Anthropic token counting endpoint for the run's model, with the same system prompt and thinking setting. Text representations are also counted with tiktoken o200k_base (representation string alone; fixed prompt = system prompt + user text with an empty page slot). For the screenshot, representation_tokens_api = usage.input_tokens of the actual call - count_tokens(empty-page prompt).
protocol.act_target_format: target is a list of CSS selectors, one per boundary hop: every selector but the last must match an <iframe> (descend into its document) or a shadow host (descend into its shadow root, open or closed). Each selector must match exactly one element in its scope.

location_tags.above_fold: target or answer fully inside the initial 1280x800 viewport
location_tags.below_fold: below the viewport, at most 1000px past its bottom edge
location_tags.far_below_fold: more than 1000px past the bottom edge of the viewport
location_tags.attribute_only: the answer is only in an attribute, form state or CSS class, not in visible text nodes

prompt.system: You are given one representation of a web page and one task about that page. Use only the information in the representation. Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else.
prompt.user_template:
<page>
{PAGE}
</page>

Task ({TASK_TYPE}): {TASK}

{ANSWER_FORMAT}
If the representation does not contain enough information to complete the task, reply with {"answer": null}.
prompt.page_slot_note: For the screenshot representation, {PAGE} is replaced by the PNG image block placed between the two text blocks '<page>\n' and '\n</page>...'. For text representations, {PAGE} is the representation string verbatim.

answer_formats.read: Reply in the form {"answer": "<the value, copied exactly as it appears on the page>"}.

act.raw_html: Identify the single element to click or fill. Reply in the form {"selector": "<a CSS selector that matches exactly that one element in this HTML document>"}.
act.markdown: Identify the single element to click or fill. Reply in the form {"text": "<the exact visible text or label of that element as it appears in this Markdown>", "occurrence": <1-based position of that element among elements with exactly this text, in page order; 1 if it is unique>}.
act.accessibility_tree: Identify the single element to click or fill. Reply in the form {"role": "<role, as written in the tree>", "name": "<accessible name, exactly as written in the tree>", "occurrence": <1-based position of that element among nodes with exactly this role and name, in tree order; 1 if it is unique>}.
act.indexed_dom: Identify the single element to click or fill. Reply in the form {"index": <the number shown in square brackets before that element>}.
act.stagehand_snapshot: Identify the single element to click or fill. Reply in the form {"ref": "<the id shown in square brackets before that element, e.g. 0-12>"}.
act.screenshot: Identify the single element to click or fill. Reply in the form {"x": <integer>, "y": <integer>}, the pixel coordinates of a point on that element in this 1280x800 screenshot, origin at the top-left corner.

prompt.sampling: temperature, top_p and top_k omitted (claude-sonnet-5 rejects non-default values); thinking disabled; max_tokens 512; no prompt caching; no retries
